title: A typical GPU app (C++, CUDA, OpenGL)
subtitle: A UI toolkit, host code, a kernel and a shader, each in its own language, meeting on the GPU

floors.label: you write
floors.note: four kinds of code, three languages

nodes.label: UI code
nodes.desc: The windows, sliders and menus, written with a UI toolkit. Qt draws its own widgets; Dear ImGui draws every widget itself with the GPU, as triangles, each frame.

nodes.label: Host code
nodes.desc: Allocates GPU memory, launches kernels with kernel<<<grid, block>>>(…), registers OpenGL textures with CUDA, and issues the draw calls.

nodes.label: Kernel
nodes.desc: The GPU function, in CUDA C++: a dialect with __global__, threadIdx and blockIdx. Compiled by nvcc, NVIDIA's compiler, as its own build step. Runs on NVIDIA GPUs only.

nodes.label: Shader
nodes.desc: A small program in OpenGL's shading language, compiled by the driver at run time. It samples the texture to colour the rectangle on screen.

nodes.label: Other GPUs, the CPU
nodes.desc: A CUDA kernel runs only on NVIDIA GPUs. The maths can be shared with the CPU (__host__ __device__ functions), but the launch code can't, and other GPUs need another kernel, in Metal or HIP.

nodes.label: CUDA driver
nodes.desc: Loads the compiled kernel and runs it.

nodes.label: OpenGL driver
nodes.desc: Draws the rectangle with the shader into the window's buffer.

nodes.label: GPU
nodes.desc: Thousands of threads; one per pixel here.

nodes.label: Shared buffer
nodes.desc: A pixel buffer OpenGL owns, registered with CUDA (cudaGraphicsGLRegisterBuffer). The kernel writes into it, and OpenGL turns it into a texture without it leaving the GPU.

nodes.label: Compositor
nodes.desc: The window system puts every window together, also on the GPU.

steps.note: A slider moves in the UI toolkit, written in C++.
The kernel was written in CUDA C++ and compiled ahead of time by nvcc, a separate compiler.
Host code launches it: kernel<<<grid, block>>>(…).
The GPU runs one thread per pixel.
It writes straight into a buffer shared with OpenGL. No copy to the CPU.
Host code has OpenGL turn the buffer into a texture and draw a rectangle with it.
A GLSL shader, another language, colours the rectangle from the texture.
The window's picture goes to the compositor, which also runs on the GPU.
On screen, and three languages met to do it.
A CUDA kernel runs only on NVIDIA GPUs.
The maths can be shared with the CPU through __host__ __device__ functions; the launch code can't.
Other GPUs need another kernel: Metal on Apple, HIP on AMD.
